subject: New Release of DSsim and mads

messages.author: 39f0839e8d6a4470
messages.subject: New Release of DSsim and mads
parts:
New versions of DSsim and mads were released on CRAN today.

(.zip versions to follow in a few days)

There have been major changes and bug fixes to DSsim (the distance sampling simulation package in R) and it is strongly recommended that you download the new version if you are using DSsim.

There have only been minor changes to mads (the multi-analysis distance sampling package in R, dealing with unidentified sighitng, covariate uncertainty and model uncertainty).

Happy Holidays,

Laura




Dr. L. Marshall
Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling
University of St. Andrews

parts:
Hi Adrian,

Currently DSsim requires you to provide a list for the gaps even if there are none.. looks like something I could improve in the package however and I will take a look later in the week.

To make it work at the moment use this code in addition to what you have written:

gaps <- list()
gaps[[1]] <- list(data.frame(x=0, y = 0))
region <- make.region(region.name="SantaCruz", units="m", coords = coords, gaps = gaps)

Then you can plot your region:

plot(region)

I would change the name of your region object from Region to region as Region is the class name.

As for your earlier question, you have to load the shapefile using the shapefile library and then pass in the shapefile object:

library(shapefiles)
region.shapefile <- read.shapefile("Region")
region <- make.region(region.name = "Survey Region", units = "m", shapefile = region.shapefile)

"Region" is the name of your shapefile file with no extension so you will be loading  the following 3 files into the object region.shapefile all at once: Region.shp, Region.shx and Region.dbf

Let me know if you run into any further issues.

Thanks for your feedback,

Laura



 
Dr. L. Marshall
Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling
University of St. Andrews

Hi Laura, a new question:

As what I need is to generate a population simulated in a defined region,  I assume that the basic steps are:

Make the region (done)
Creating a density object
Create a population description
Create detectability (if needed)
Generate a population instance

I assume that the next step would be to make.density, before generating a population.

In the make.density command, if density.surface is referred as a data.frame, I suppose I can read a table with data in columns x,y, and density. All of them numeric. 885.88 m is the gap between density "cells"

Then I call make.density and get the following error

Error in obj...@density.surface[[i]]$density :  $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
I attach the script. The text file is quite large however I can send it to you at your request.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
coords <- gaps <- list()

gaps[[1]] <- list(data.frame(x=0, y = 0))
region <- make.region(region.name="SantaCruz", units="m", coords = coords, gaps = gaps)

plot(region)

densidad.pred <-read.delim("density.txt", sep = "\t", header=T, dec=",")
densidad.pred$x<-as.numeric(densidad.pred$x)
densidad.pred$y<-as.numeric(densidad.pred$y)
densidad.pred$density<-as.numeric(densidad.pred$density)

make.density(region.obj=region, density.surface = densidad.pred, 885.88, 885.88)
 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

messages.author: 39f0839e8d6a4470
messages.subject: Re: New Release of DSsim and mads
parts:
Hi Adrian,

Apoligies there is a mistake in the help file, I will get that ammended ASAP.

The density.surface argument to the make.density command should be a list of dataframes with one dataframe for each strata. The dataframes should have columns x, y and density as you have created. The following should work:

densidad.list <- list()
densidad.list[[1]] <- densidad.pred
make.density(region.obj=region, density.surface = densidad.list, 885.88, 885.88)

The detectability object is not optional it is required by the simulation. This determines the probability of detecting the animals based on their distance from the transect and allows the DSsim so simulate detections.

After you have defined the region, density, population and detectability you can create an instance of a population. However, it is easier to create the simulation object as a whole and then do what you want with it: generate.population, generate.transects, create.survey.results, run. The other oject you will need before you can create the simulation is the analysis list object, created using make.ddf.analysis.list(...).

Laura





 
Dr. L. Marshall
Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling
University of St. Andrews
